extracted.intended_audience: communication officers, implementing partners and contractors responsible for EU-funded external actions (projects, programmes, grants, contracts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, producing and checking communication and visibility materials for European Union external actions (projects/programmes funded by the EU). Covers mandatory visibility elements, templates, approval and reporting obligations, and good-practice message and media guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the EU emblem and graphic identity
rubrics_metrics.description: All communication materials and visibility items must use the EU emblem/flag and conform to the EU graphic identity requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes when and how to reproduce the EU emblem (proportions, clear space, colours), what other logos may appear alongside it, and prohibitions on altering or animating the emblem. Examples show correct/incorrect uses and minimum size/contrast recommendations. Anti-patterns: cropping, recolouring, or placing other visual elements on top of the emblem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory funding acknowledgement statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications, web pages, press releases, events and other materials must acknowledge EU funding with a standard sentence (e.g., 'This project is funded by the European Union' or the contractual equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual specifies exact wording to be used (or contract-specific phrasing), languages where applicable, and where on the material the acknowledgement should appear. It gives examples for print, web and multimedia. Omitting the acknowledgement or using informal variants is flagged as non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the 'views expressed' disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Where required, materials must include the disclaimer that the views expressed are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of the European Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance indicates when the disclaimer is mandatory (e.g., for evaluation reports, studies, public statements by partners), preferred placement and exact legal phrasing, and examples. Anti-patterns include weakening the disclaimer language or omitting it when specified by contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo placement, size and co-branding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for placement and sizing of the EU emblem relative to partners' logos, and instructions on co-branding with other funders or implementers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes clear-space rules, minimum sizes for print and screen, ordering of logos, and compatibility rules for co-financers. Examples of approved logo layouts and unacceptable co-branding (e.g., making partner logos more prominent than the EU emblem) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility requirements for printed materials and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed outputs (leaflets, reports, posters, brochures) funded by the EU must follow prescribed visibility elements (emblem, acknowledgement, contact details, date and disclaimer where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual gives page-placement examples, minimum type sizes, required elements for covers and back covers, and checklists for printers. It flags common errors like missing credits, incorrect colour reproduction, or failure to include the funding sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Websites and online content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project and programme websites must display the EU emblem and the funding acknowledgement prominently and follow online-branding rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recommended placement (homepage and project pages), acceptable links to the EU website, rules for social media profile headers, requirements for metadata or alt text, and procedures for obtaining prior approval or notifying the contracting authority about websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release content and format guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases about EU-funded activities should follow a clear structure and include mandatory visibility lines, contact information and accurate attribution of EU funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended structure: headline, summary, key facts (what, where, when, who, how much), quote(s), background information, EU funding acknowledgement and media contact. Guidance stresses factual accuracy, non-political tone, and using the exact acknowledgement wording. Examples of good and bad press releases are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography, captions and photo-credit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Photos used in communications must show the EU emblem when relevant, include accurate captions, and carry photographer/owner credits and copyright information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual explains consent and release forms, minimum caption content (who/what/where/when), when to include the funding acknowledgement in image captions, recommended resolution and file formats, and credit-line examples. Anti-patterns: using images without permission, poor-quality images, or missing credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event and ceremony visibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Events financed by the EU (launches, inaugurations, handovers) must ensure visible EU recognition (banners, backdrops, podium signage, and speaking lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what visibility items must be present on-site (flag, roll-ups, press walls), the wording for event materials, guidance for guest introductions and speaker acknowledgements, and required photographic coverage. It includes examples of compliant stage/backdrop setups and prohibited practices (e.g., hiding the EU emblem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signage and plaques at project sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical project sites must display durable plaques or billboards acknowledging EU support, following size, content and installation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers mandatory content (emblem, funding sentence, project title, contract number, implementing partner), minimum dimensions/materials, placement near the site, and maintenance requirements. It explains when temporary vs permanent signage is required and how to report installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Templates, visuals and multimodal outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual supplies and mandates use of standard templates for brochures, posters, presentations, videos and multi-media products to ensure consistent EU visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which templates are mandatory, how to adapt them (language, photographs, logos), and technical specs (video intro/outro with emblem, captioning/subtitles). Includes examples and guidance on avoiding template misuse (altering emblem or removing acknowledgement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval, clearance and contractual compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain communication outputs require prior approval by the contracting authority or must meet contractual visibility clauses and reporting obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies materials that need prior approval (e.g., large publicity campaigns, websites, press events), timelines for submission, content of clearance requests, and documentation to be kept for audits. Non-compliance consequences and corrective actions are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media messaging and behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media posts and campaigns should acknowledge EU funding where appropriate, use approved visuals and avoid political messaging that conflicts with EU policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on wording, hashtags, use of logos in profile/cover images, tagging EU institutional accounts, crisis/social-sensitivity rules, and archiving social outputs. Examples show compliant post templates and pitfalls (misleading claims, unapproved sponsorship language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-financing, partner attribution and logo hierarchies
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple donors or partners contribute, the manual prescribes how to attribute each actor and how to order logos and acknowledgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains ordering rules (EU prominence where specified), wording for co-financed projects, and how to present partner contributions without diminishing EU visibility. Includes examples for mixed-funder posters and multi-partner events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message quality: clarity, relevance and non-partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication should be clear, targeted to the audience, accurate, culturally sensitive and non-partisan, avoiding advocacy that conflicts with EU neutrality rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on audience segmentation, key message development, use of plain language, measurement of impact, and examples of inappropriate political or promotional language. Recommends fact-checking and coordination with EU delegations for sensitive topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, documentation and reporting of visibility activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementers must document visibility actions (photos, press clippings, links, distribution lists) and report them as part of contractual monitoring and final reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists required documentation (signed attendance lists, high-resolution photos with captions, copies of publications, links to online coverage), recommended reporting formats and frequency, and examples of evidence accepted during audits. Advises keeping originals for a contracted period.
